name: Fenwick Abara-Szymański
role: Noodle cart vendor, Edison Grid district
location: Edison Grid, corner of Copper Row and the 14th underpass, near Armitage and Milwaukee
description:
Fenwick is a lean, unhurried man of medium height with deep umber skin and close-cropped hair that he keeps dyed a matte rust-red. He has a bioluminescent mod along his forearms — thin lines of blue-white light under the skin that pulse gently with his heartbeat, which he originally got because it helped him keep time when cooking stock. He wears the same canvas apron every day, bleached and re-stained so many times it has developed a geological stratigraphy of meals past. His cart, 'The Long Burn,' is a retrofitted maintenance vehicle he rebuilt himself over eighteen months, and he knows its every rattle and squeak as personally as a language.

Fenwick moves through the world with a quality of stillness that some people mistake for slowness and others, correctly, read as patience. He is not a talker — his cart is not a place for conversation so much as a place for eating — but he notices everything: who looks hungry versus broke, who's been crying, who's scanning the crowd too carefully. He keeps a small E.L.F. shrine rigged into the cart's boiler panel, a data-spirit he calls 'the Pilot Light' to whom he murmurs thanks each morning before ignition.

core_fears: His daughter growing up not knowing him
The cart being impounded or destroyed — losing the one thing he built from nothing
core_desires: Stability — a day that goes as planned
Being the kind of father his own wasn't
coping_mechanisms: The ritual of cooking as a way to feel in control
Emotional withdrawal — going quiet rather than engaging conflict
blind_spots: Believes being present physically is the same as being emotionally available
Underestimates how much his silences communicate
psychology.secret: He witnessed a Axiom security officer disposing of something in the underpass canal eight months ago and has said nothing. He told himself it wasn't his business. He's been telling himself that for eight months.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Minimal, functional, with occasional bursts of unexpected precision about food, temperature, or timing
speech_patterns.cadence: Slow and considered — he doesn't fill silences
verbal_tics: Referring to his cart in the first person plural: 'we're out of the pork belly'
example_lines: 'Broth's been going since four. You can taste it.'
'I don't know what you saw. I was cooking.'

story_hooks: Whatever Fenwick saw in the underpass canal is now relevant ��� someone is asking around the Edison Grid, and his regulars are starting to notice
His daughter has gone quiet and he can't reach her; he'll ask someone he trusts from the cart — obliquely, carefully — to check on her
narrative_function: Reliable scene-setting presence; a node of quiet observation in a busy district. Information source who never seems like one — people talk near his cart as if he's furniture. Can point players toward things he's witnessed without ever seeming to inform.
augmentations: Bioluminescent subdermal lines on forearms (blue-white, heartbeat-synced). No other mods.
daily_life: Rolls the cart out at 0530 for morning workers, breaks midday, returns for the evening shift until 2200. Spends Sunday mornings sourcing ingredients and visiting his daughter at his ex-partner's apartment in Calumet Rise.
affiliation: Independent; informal supplier relationship with Grainfort wholesale district

decision_rules: Don't get involved in things that put the cart at risk
Feed people who are hungry regardless of whether they can pay — but only once
escalation_ladder: A single quiet statement of boundary
Packing up and leaving — removing himself entirely

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Neutral and efficient — takes the order, makes the food, asks no questions
interpersonal_modes.friends: Slightly warmer — remembers orders, nods, might offer an extra portion without comment

stress_responses.low: Cooks with more focus, becomes very precise
stress_responses.medium: Goes completely nonverbal, communicates only in gestures
stress_responses.high: Leaves. Physically removes himself from the situation.

contradictions: Prizes stability above all but has built his life on a cart with wheels — he could leave any time, which is the point
habits: Wipes the counter three times before opening
Always gives the last bowl of the day away free, regardless of who's there
breaking_points: Someone threatening or damaging the cart
Being forced to choose between his daughter and his silence about what he saw

physical_description.build: Lean and wiry, muscular forearms from years of stirring heavy stock pots and pushing the cart through Edison Grid's cracked streets. No excess fat; his body is efficient.
physical_description.hair_color: Matte rust-red (dyed; natural color likely dark brown or black)
physical_description.eye_color: Dark brown with fine laugh lines at the corners
physical_description.complexion: Weathered but clean, marked by years of steam and heat exposure. Faint scars on knuckles from knife work. Face carries the still quality of someone who listens more than speaks.
distinguishing_marks: Bioluminescent subdermal lines running along both forearms in thin parallel trails, glowing soft blue-white in rhythm with heartbeat — visible when sleeves are rolled or pushed up
Thin burn scar on the inside of left wrist, old and faded, likely from early cooking accident
Calloused hands with permanent discoloration from years of handling turmeric and other spices
physical_description.visible_augmentations: Bioluminescent forearm mods only — thin blue-white lines beneath the skin that pulse steadily. Most visible when arms are bare or when ambient light drops in the evening shifts.
physical_description.posture_movement: Moves with deliberate economy. Stands still frequently, observing rather than fidgeting. When working the cart, movements are precise and rhythmic — choreographed by repetition. Does not rush. Carries a quality of groundedness even in crowded grid intersections.
physical_description.clothing_style: The same bleached canvas apron daily, layered with the stains of hundreds of meals — a geological record of his work. Beneath it: simple tier-4 workwear (faded gray or black thermal, worn jeans, steel-toed boots suitable for standing 16+ hours). No corporate logos. Everything practical, nothing decorative. Moves like someone who owns very little and maintains what he has.

image_prompt: A lean 34-year-old man of mixed West African and Polish heritage, deep umber skin, close-cropped matte rust-red hair, standing still beside a retrofitted noodle cart in dim industrial lighting. Medium height, wiry build, weathered hands. Both forearms glow with soft blue-white bioluminescent lines pulsing gently with heartbeat, visible beneath the skin. Wearing a heavily stained canvas apron layered with the geological record of countless meals, simple thermal shirt, worn jeans. Dark brown eyes with laugh lines, weathered but clean complexion. Standing in Edison Grid at dusk near a warehouse underpass, surrounded by neon signs reflecting off wet pavement, steam rising from the cart. Mood: patient, observant, grounded. Soft blue-white bio-glow accent lighting. Cyberpunk, lived-in, working-class realism. --ar 2:3 --v 6
